worked_solution:
The general solution near a regular singular point $x=0$ of a second-order homogeneous linear differential equation with indicial roots ${\lambda }_{1}\ge {\lambda }_{2}$ is given by

$$
y={c}_{1}{y}_{1}(x)+{c}_{2}{y}_{2}(x),
$$

where

- ${y}_{1}(x)={x}^{{\lambda }_{1}}{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}({\lambda }_{1}){x}^{n}$ is the first Frobenius solution corresponding to the larger root of the indicial equation, and

- ${a}_{n}({\lambda }_{1})$ are the coefficients produced by the method when $\lambda ={\lambda }_{1}.$

We are given that the indicial equation is $3{\lambda }^{2}-\lambda =0.$
Solving for the roots, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{\lambda }^{2}-\lambda  & =0 \\ \lambda (3\lambda -1) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =0,\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The larger solution is ${\lambda }_{1}=\frac{1}{3}.$ Therefore, the first Frobenius series solution we take is

$$
{y}_{1}(x)={x}^{1/3}{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}.
$$

With $\lambda =\frac{1}{3},$ the recurrence relation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =\frac{4}{(\frac{1}{3}+n)(3(\frac{1}{3}+n)-1)}\,{a}_{n-1} \\  & =\frac{4}{(n+\frac{1}{3})(3n)}\,{a}_{n-1} \\  & =\frac{4}{n(3n+1)}\,{a}_{n-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, with ${a}_{0}\ne 0$ arbitrary, we evaluate the first three coefficients using the given recurrence relation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & \ne 0, \\ {a}_{1} & =\frac{4}{1(3\cdot 1+1)}\,{a}_{0}={a}_{0}, \\ {a}_{2} & =\frac{4}{2(3\cdot 2+1)}\,{a}_{1}=\frac{2}{7}\,{a}_{1}=\frac{2}{7}{a}_{0}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the first Frobenius solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}(x) & ={x}^{1/3}{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n} \\  & ={x}^{1/3}({a}_{0}+{a}_{0}x+\frac{2}{7}{a}_{0}{x}^{2}+⋯) \\  & ={a}_{0}({x}^{1/3}+{x}^{4/3}+\frac{2}{7}{x}^{7/3}+⋯).\end{aligned}
$$

The general solution near a regular singular point x=0 of a second-order homogeneous linear differential equation with indicial roots λ1≥λ2 is given by y=c1y1(x)+c2y2(x), where

  • y1(x)=xλ1∑n=0∞an(λ1)xn is the first Frobenius solution corresponding to the larger root of the indicial equation, and

  • an(λ1) are the coefficients produced by the method when λ=λ1.

We are given that the indicial equation is 3λ2−λ=0. Solving for the roots, we get

3λ2−λ=0λ(3λ−1)=0λ=0,13

The larger solution is λ1=13. Therefore, the first Frobenius series solution we take is

y1(x)=x1/3∑n=0∞anxn.

With λ=13, the recurrence relation is given by

an=4(13+n)(3(13+n)−1)an−1=4(n+13)(3n)an−1=4n(3n+1)an−1.

Now, with a0≠0 arbitrary, we evaluate the first three coefficients using the given recurrence relation as follows:

a0≠0,a1=41(3⋅1+1)a0=a0,a2=42(3⋅2+1)a1=27a1=27a0.

Therefore, the first Frobenius solution is

y1(x)=x1/3∑n=0∞anxn=x1/3(a0+a0x+27a0x2+⋯)=a0(x1/3+x4/3+27x7/3+⋯).
